children: Citi expects lithium prices to remain weak in the near term, underpinned by supply chain destocking. Prices have fallen by as much as 40% since early September--raising the key question of whether correction has run its course, Citi says. "Recent channel checks by our China Battery Materials team have not been encouraging," it says. Consumers are likely to defer purchases and maintain lean inventories, meaning risks are skewed to the downside until either supply is cut or downstream stockpiles are depleted, says the bank. It downgrades its 0-3 month price target for lithium carbonate to $12,000/metric ton from $20,000/ton. Its target for lithium hydroxide also falls to $12,000/ton, from $17,000/ton, while its target for spodumene concentrate drops to $1,200/ton from $2,000/ton. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
